rationale.Physical Exam: Genitalia / Pelvic: Cervical motion tenderness + adnexal tenderness + purulent discharge = classic PID.
rationale.Urinalysis / Urine culture: Rule out UTI/pyelo — dysuria can overlap.
rationale.Chlamydia / Gonorrhea NAAT: Identify causative organisms. NAAT on cervical swab or urine.
rationale.HCG, beta (pregnancy test): MUST rule out ectopic pregnancy — can mimic PID.
rationale.Pelvic ultrasound: Rule out tubo-ovarian abscess. Transvaginal preferred.
rationale.Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 14 days: Covers chlamydia. 14-day course for PID (not 7-day like uncomplicated CT).
rationale.Advise patient, sexual partner needs tre: Partner treatment essential to prevent reinfection.
rationale.Doxycycline x 7 days only: PID requires 14-day course, not the 7-day course used for uncomplicated chlamydia. Inadequate duration risks treatment failure and complications.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a sexually active young woman presenting with bilateral lower abdominal/pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness, purulent cervical discharge, fever, and leukocytosis. Pelvic inflammatory disease is an ascending infection from the lower genital tract — commonly Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, though polymicrobial. Diagnosis is clinical based on CDC criteria: uterine/adnexal tenderness + cervical motion tenderness (minimum). Complications: tubo-ovarian abscess, infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain. Treatment: empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics covering chlamydia, gonorrhea, and anaerobes — ceftriaxone 250mg IM once + doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 14 days + metronidazole 500mg PO BID x 14 days. Partner treatment essential. Screen for other STIs. Admit if severe, TOA, pregnant, or failed outpatient treatment.
